correctness.rationale: The atom-respecting bisimulation signature follows exactly from accessibility being an equivalence relation. Labelled enumeration is bijective. The Bell ratio contraction identities supply E[T], E[T(T-1)], E[H], and E[N1(N1-1)]. Second moments give T/(n log n)->1/2. A dependency-graph Chen–Stein bound conditional on the sampled partition and vanishing duplicate-block-support risk give the Poisson critical window. Pairwise-independent edge-collision indicators prove subcritical failure, and first-moment bounds prove the supercritical side. Bundled independent modal-refinement enumeration agrees with generating-function DP in 20 exhaustive finite cases; finite cases do not substitute for asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The n log n threshold is the first-order critical vocabulary size for preserving every state under modal-bisimulation contraction when the underlying epistemic partition itself is uniformly random. The nondegenerate e^{-1/(2 theta)} window quantifies the transition rather than merely bounding it. The cross-block-support obstruction requires an additional argument beyond ordinary birthday collisions. This natural semantic invariant and its sharp asymptotic answer motivate the exact sampling problem.
